clue.text: What one needs to succeed with a flying machine, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the flying machine's name is only spoken, matching another spelling in sound

parts.note: an airship is a flying machine, a dirigible balloon

explanation.surface: A would-be aviator wonders what equipment success requires.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken, AIRSHIP and HEIRSHIP are alike, since the H of 'heir' is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: To succeed to a title or estate one must be the rightful inheritor, which is the status named.

clue.text: Bill's backer

parts.note: a bill of exchange is backed by someone signing its reverse; it also looks like a supporter of a man called Bill

explanation.definitionFit: One who signs the back of a bill of exchange guarantees it, literally backing it.

clue.text: More life policies — they boost confidence

definitions.meaning: words of comfort that restore someone's belief

explanation.surface: An insurer's extra cover leaves clients feeling more secure.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance is life insurance, so further policies are re-assurances, while comforting words that steady nerves share the spelling.

clue.text: Nadir? Cheer up, old vixen!

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the whole run of letters is read from the bottom

parts.note: taken as written
rah is a cheer

explanation.surface: Someone at their lowest point is told to cheer up by an old shrew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses NADIR + RAH. Vixen here is a bad-tempered woman, not a fox.
explanation.definitionFit: A harridan is a bossy, scolding woman, the same insult as a shrewish vixen.

clue.text: Daring newsmen surround town centre

indicators.note: surround says the word for newsmen wraps around another piece

parts.note: the press is journalists collectively

indicators.note: centre picks the middle letters of town

explanation.surface: Bold reporters close in on the middle of a town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes OW from tOWn; 'surround' puts it inside PRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Prowess is skill or bravery, a noun sense of daring as boldness.

clue.text: This accelerator gets us in real trouble

indicators.note: trouble suggests the letters of in and real are disturbed and reshuffled

explanation.surface: A particle machine lands us in real difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges IN + REAL; 'gets us' is a link. A particle accelerator is commonly named for its straight-line design.
explanation.definitionFit: A linac or linear accelerator drives particles along a straight track, so the word names the accelerator type.

clue.text: I have money put up by Jacobson

indicators.note: in a down clue, put up by means placed above the other piece

parts.note: the lev is the currency of Bulgaria

explanation.surface: A man named Jacobson is lent cash by the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jacobson' is read as Jacob's son: Levi was the third son of Jacob in Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Levi was one of the twelve sons of the patriarch Jacob, so a son of Jacob.

clue.text: Go for gold? That's the view

definitions.meaning: to search for gold deposits in the ground
an outlook or scene from a vantage point

explanation.surface: An athlete is urged to aim for first place, and someone agrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Miners searching for ore prospect, and a wide scene before one is a prospect.

clue.text: Transports of delight for children at Christmas

definitions.text: Transports of delight for children at Christmas

parts.words: Transports of delight for children at Christmas
parts.note: transports read literally: the animals that pull Santa's sleigh, bringing joy to children on Christmas Eve

explanation.walkthrough: 'Transports of delight' usually means raptures; here the transports are the beasts hauling the sleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Santa's sleigh is drawn by antlered Arctic deer, the vehicles of children's festive delight.

clue.text: Append note returning Scandinavian work

indicators.note: returning means the joined letters for append and note are read backwards

parts.note: to append is to add
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Someone attaches a note to a piece of Nordic writing sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns ADD + E into EDDA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic collection of Norse myths and poems, a Scandinavian literary work.

clue.text: Brewer's art is in mixing fruit

indicators.note: mixing tells us the letters of the brewer's art phrase are stirred into a new order

parts.note: the S of the possessive is kept as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A brewer's craft lies in blending fruit into the beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixing' rearranges BREWERSARTIS into the twelve-letter answer; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Strawberries are soft red summer berries, a common fruit.

clue.text: Indian tree-swinger doctors find bloody interesting

definitions.text: Indian tree-swinger doctors find bloody interesting

parts.words: Indian tree-swinger doctors find bloody interesting
parts.note: a South Asian primate whose name was given to a blood factor discovered by medical researchers

explanation.walkthrough: The Rh blood group factor was named after the macaque in which it was first found, so doctors find its blood interesting literally.
explanation.definitionFit: This macaque of India swings through trees and gave its name to the Rh blood factor.

clue.text: Published, one's taken to court

parts.note: one is I, and one's gives I'S, read as IS
someone taken to court has been sued

explanation.surface: An author whose book came out finds themself facing a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something issued has been put out or released to the public, as a published book is.

clue.text: Schoolboy's plea heard during a caning?

definitions.text: Schoolboy's plea heard during a caning?

parts.words: Schoolboy's plea heard during a caning?
parts.note: a boy being beaten would cry 'Sir, cease!', which sounds like a word for a halt or end

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sir, cease!' run together gives the sound of this old word meaning cessation, exactly what the boy is begging for.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an archaic term for a stopping or respite, the relief a punished pupil wants.

clue.text: Decrees giving gold to Danes, we hear

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

indicators.note: we hear signals that the Danes are only spoken, giving a word of the same sound

parts.note: people of Denmark

explanation.surface: Rulings are issued that hand treasure over to the Danish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving' is a link; OR plus the sound of DANES spelt DAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To ordain is to order or decree officially, so the plural verb matches decrees.

clue.text: Busy with tenants

definitions.meaning: engaged or taken up with something
having people living in it, as a let house

explanation.surface: A landlord is kept busy with renters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone engrossed is fully engaged, and a building with residents is inhabited: both senses share one word.

clue.text: Release numbers one found in dull surroundings

indicators.note: found in says the following pieces sit within another word
surroundings says the word for dull wraps around the other pieces

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not shiny
NUM is short for numbers, as in the Book of Numbers
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: A figure is let go after being discovered in drab surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: NUM + I go inside MAT. The answer is a rare verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To manumit is to free a slave from bondage, a formal setting at liberty.

clue.text: Conformist articles about origins of general liturgy in churches

indicators.note: about says the two articles sit around the other letters

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a second indefinite article an

indicators.note: origins of takes the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A traditionalist's writings deal with the roots of church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'origins of' gives GLIC; 'about' puts it between AN and AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Church of England were historically the conformists, as opposed to dissenting Nonconformists.

clue.text: Hard goods offered by mail order catalogue, say ?

definitions.text: Hard goods offered by mail order catalogue, say ?

parts.words: Hard goods offered by mail order catalogue, say ?
parts.note: metal goods, the sort of hardware sold in a mail order list; chain mail is itself made of metal

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard goods' hints at hardware, and 'mail' at armour made of metal links.
explanation.definitionFit: These are household articles of metal, the hardware a catalogue might sell.

clue.text: The way for bargees to benefit from HP

definitions.text: The way for bargees to benefit from HP

parts.words: The way for bargees to benefit from HP
parts.note: HP is horsepower: canal boats were hauled by horses walking a path along the bank

explanation.walkthrough: HP looks like hire purchase, a British credit plan, but is horsepower: horses pulled barges along the canal bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The path beside a canal let horses haul barges, so it was the boatmen's horse-powered route.

clue.text: Music to study ? Sure thing, love

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a cert is a certainty, a sure thing in betting
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A student asks whether music helps revision and is answered with warm confidence.
explanation.definitionFit: A concerto is a classical composition for soloist and orchestra, a piece of music.

clue.text: Seldom depend on support of the Academy

indicators.note: in a down clue, the support of a piece sits beneath it

parts.note: RA is the Royal Academy of Arts
to rely is to depend on

explanation.surface: An artist rarely leans on the backing of the Academy.
explanation.walkthrough: RELY is placed under RA, holding it up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means not often, a synonym of seldom.

clue.text: Put back this ham — we shall have game

definitions.text: Put back this ham — we shall have game

parts.words: Put back this ham — we shall have game
parts.note: a cured leg of pork; put the word 'back' before it and you have a board game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' plus the answer is the name of a dice-and-board game, so the clue is a playful cryptic definition rather than a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a cured hindquarter of bacon pig, a kind of ham, and the second half of a board game's name.

clue.text: Banishment for writing one, and no return

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
script is handwriting
the Roman numeral I is one

indicators.note: return says the little word no is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone is exiled for writing a single piece and may never come back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' is a link; 'return' turns NO into ON at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Proscription is outlawing or exile, a formal banishment.

clue.text: Cry of pain, if a bit touchy

indicators.note: a bit says only a part of the word touchy is used, its letters lying inside it

explanation.surface: Someone yelps when they are even slightly sensitive.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits in tOUCHy; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is what people shout when hurt, an interjection of pain.

clue.text: Hammerstones sounds a hot tip

indicators.note: sounds says the racing word is spoken, with a silent-K word of the same sound entered

parts.note: a nap is a racing tipster's most confident selection of the day

explanation.surface: A stone-breaker is told about a sure winner at the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hammerstones' is 'hammers stones', a verb phrase. NAP is British racing slang for the tipster's best bet of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: To knap is to strike flints or stones with a hammer to shape them.

clue.text: Laces with hot variety of onion

indicators.note: variety suggests a different form of the letters of laces and hot, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone spikes laces with a hot type of onion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' scrambles LACES + HOT; 'with' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: An eschalot is an old name for the shallot, a small mild member of the allium family.

clue.text: For whom Yeats planned Innisfree accommodation

definitions.text: For whom Yeats planned Innisfree accommodation

parts.words: For whom Yeats planned Innisfree accommodation
parts.note: in The Lake Isle of Innisfree, Yeats will have 'a hive for' a buzzing insect besides his bean-rows

explanation.walkthrough: Yeats's poem The Lake Isle of Innisfree has the line 'Nine bean-rows will I have there, a hive for the honey-bee.'
explanation.definitionFit: The poem's hive is built for a nectar-gathering insect, the one housed in the planned accommodation.
